answer: A defense ties each agent identity to a refundable bond and a reputation ledger, not a free username. To join, an agent locks a bond that is slashed if peers prove fraud or duplicate identities. Like a sonnet, the rules are strict: every job is signed, recorded, and checked by unrelated verifiers, so reputation grows only through attested work. An attacker wanting a hundred fake agents must post a hundred bonds and fund a hundred histories. A single ember of fraud can burn the bond and taint the cluster, while a crystal-clear audit trail shows that cost before anyone trusts a new identity.
